tech_debt.description: First-row insert race (theoretical): SELECT FOR UPDATE LIMIT 1 acquires no lock when WHERE matches 0 rows. Two concurrent sessions inserting the FIRST-EVER ledger row for the same (design, grade) can each succeed at running_balance=delta instead of [delta, 2·delta]. Spec-compliant with DS-002 + LLD; PRD silent; TC-087 assumes pre-existing row. V2 mitigation options: lock master row, advisory locks, unique+retry.

tech_debt.description: Frontend tests TC-092/093/095/097/099/101/102 (7) cannot exercise Radix UI Select / Popover interactions in jsdom — portals + internal state machinery don't fully materialize. Matches the S1 pattern (TC-045 deferred for same root cause). 6 zod-direct sibling TCs in the same files pass cleanly. Resolution options: (a) mock @radix-ui/react-select with native <select> shim, (b) move to Playwright/Cypress E2E in S3+, (c) accept as scaffold-level coverage (backend tests cover the same ACs via API integration).

DS-002 race discovered + closed by /ases-system-test S2 ST-007. Root cause: PG SELECT ... LIMIT 1 ORDER BY ... FOR UPDATE does NOT re-resolve LIMIT after waiting on a row lock — the waiter re-reads the originally-identified row, missing the newly-inserted latest row from the holder. Fixed by adding pg_advisory_xact_lock(design_id, grade_id) BEFORE the FOR UPDATE in src/domain/stock.py::_apply. DS-002 spec text could be amended in S3 to mandate the advisory-lock-first pattern.
